_explanation.purpose: EXAMPLE TEMPLATE - shows correct format for writing scenarios with optional examples for data-driven testing
_explanation.scenario_structure: scenarios array: each has name, sequential_order, type (happy_path/edge_case/error_case), steps (single newline-delimited string of Given/When/Then), background (array), test_method, and optional examples
_explanation.steps_format: steps is a SINGLE STRING with newline separators. NOT an array of objects. Example: "Given state exists\nWhen action occurs\nThen outcome is observed"
_explanation.background_format: background is an ARRAY (empty [] when no shared setup). When used with examples, background holds shared Given/And steps as strings in the array.
_explanation.examples_structure: Scenario-level examples hold ONLY scenario-specific tables. Each table has name, columns, rows.
_explanation.variable_matching: Every <variable_name> in steps MUST appear in example columns. Include both input variables and expected output/result variables
_explanation.domain_alignment: Example tables MUST mirror domain_concepts structure: each domain concept with collaborators becomes a related table, responsibilities define the columns
_explanation.use_case: Reference this template when writing scenarios to see correct Gherkin format and Examples table structure
_explanation.context_source: REQUIRED on scenarios and examples - traces knowledge to source document, page, section, or conversation. Format: {file, page, section} or {type: 'chat'|'code'|'inferred', description}

scenarios.name: Simple scenario without examples
scenarios.steps:
Given {Concept} exists with valid state
When admin performs action on {Concept}
Then {Concept} is updated
And confirmation is displayed

scenarios.name: Scenario with flat examples
Error scenario
scenarios.steps:
Given {Concept} has invalid data
When admin submits {Concept}
Then error message is displayed
And {Concept} is not saved

scenarios.name: Scenario with hierarchical domain-aligned examples
scenarios.steps:
Given Customer "<customer_name>" has account "<account_number>"
And Account belongs to product "<product_name>"
And Account has transactions shown in table
When Customer looks up account
Then Customer sees transactions for "<product_name>"
And Customer sees "<expected_outcome>"
